title: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of Efficiency in Conformalized Regression
claim: A target error is decomposed by the triangle inequality into separately bounded terms that together give the overall convergence rate.
layout: 1 panel, top-to-bottom derivation, braces under terms, shaded rate boxes

The top line, in a gray box, is the expected absolute difference between the conformal interval length |C(X)| and the oracle length |C*(X)|. An equality expands it into quantile terms. A triangle-inequality line then splits it into four additive terms joined by plus signs. Each term has a black underbrace and a gray-shaded O(·) rate below it. abstract: Conformal prediction provides prediction sets with coverage guarantees. The informativeness of conformal prediction depends on its efficiency, typically quantified by the expected size of the prediction set. Prior work on the efficiency of conformalized regression commonly treats the miscoverage level $Î±$ as a fixed constant. In this work, we establish non-asymptotic bounds on the deviation of the prediction set length from the oracle interval length for conformalized quantile and median regression trained via SGD, under mild assumptions on the data distribution. Our bounds of order $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{n} + 1/(Î±^2 n) + 1/\sqrt{m} + \exp(-Î±^2 m))$ capture the joint dependence of efficiency on the proper training set size $n$, the calibration set size $m$, and the miscoverage level $Î±$. The results identify phase transitions in convergence rates across different regimes of $Î±$, offering guidance for allocating data to control excess prediction set length. Empirical results are consistent with our theoretical findings.
